newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ROMATEX LOW SALE PRICE SURPRISES ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: ROMATEX LOW SALE PRICE SURPRISES ANALYSTS.

text.p: South Africa's Consolidated Frame Textiles Ltd (Confram) has bought fellow clothing and textile company Romatex Ltd for a steal, analysts said on Monday, expressing surprise at the low sale price.
They were responding to an announcement earlier on Monday that Confram would buy 50.8 percent of Romatex at 2.25 rand a share, a discount of 75 percent to Romatex's net asset value of almost 10 rand.

"The market more or less expected a low price, after the cautionary last week... People said maybe three rand (per share), but never as low as 2.25 rand," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
"Confram got a good deal, but Romatex was given away to them," he added.
Romatex and its parent C.G. Smith Ltd last week said any bid for the textile company would be at less than 330 cents a share.

Analysts said Confram was able to secure such an attractive price most likely due to Romatex's poor trading performance in the current financial year and the troubled state of the South African textile and clothing industry.
"It's the whole thing about the state of the textile and clothing industry, that's why they (C.G. Smith) got such a poor deal," another analyst said.
South African clothing and textile companies have been hard hit in the past few years by a flood of illegal imports.
A further blow was a week long wage strike in July which cost both employers and workers millions of rands in lost wages and production.
The announcement on Monday said the sale price reflected the trading performance of Romatex in the year to end-September 1996 with the company expected to make a small loss in the second six months.
Full year results, which were seen just above breakeven, will be announced on October 31.

According to the deal announced on Monday, Confram would buy shares equal to 19.3 percent of Romatex from C.G. Smith at 225 cents a share. C.G. Smith would in turn have acquired these shares from Associated Furniture Companies Ltd .

Confram would then extend an offer to Romatex shareholders to buy 38.0 percent of their shareholding at 225 cents per Romatex share. Should shareholders not accept this offer, C.G. Smith had undertaken to provide the necessary top-up shares for Confram to end up with a 50.8 percent stake in Romatex.

Romatex shares were last trading 10 cents or three percent weaker at 320 cents. Analysts said shares were unlikely to fall below three rand as much of the bad news had already been discounted last week when stocks fell from 550 cents to 330. The company was also seen improving its trading performance in the 1996/97 financial year.
Confram shares were unchanged at 540 cents.
